dictionary_fields.name: algorithm
dictionary_fields.description: DNSSEC algorithm number carried by the record (IANA DNSSEC Algorithm Numbers). Algorithm 0 in CDS/CDNSKEY is the RFC 8078 delete signal.

dictionary_fields.name: digest_type
dictionary_fields.description: DS/CDS digest type (1 = SHA-1, 2 = SHA-256, 4 = SHA-384).

dictionary_fields.name: dnskey_protocol
dictionary_fields.description: DNSKEY/CDNSKEY protocol octet. RFC 4034 s2.1.2 fixes it at 3, so this evidences the RFC 4034 record format specifically rather than DNSSEC in general.

dictionary_fields.name: domain
dictionary_fields.description: Fully qualified domain name that was queried.

dictionary_fields.name: flags
dictionary_fields.description: DNSKEY/NSEC3 flags field, rendered as a string. Only reliably exported in later measurement generations.

dictionary_fields.name: key_tag
dictionary_fields.description: DNSSEC key tag identifying the key a DS/RRSIG/CDS record refers to.

dictionary_fields.name: measurement_id
dictionary_fields.description: Opaque identifier of the individual measurement run or object the row came from.

dictionary_fields.name: nsec3_flags
dictionary_fields.description: NSEC3 flags as an integer. Bit 0 is Opt-Out (RFC 5155 s6): when set, unsigned delegations may be skipped in the hash chain. Distinct from the generic `flags` field, which is a string coalesced across DNSKEY/CDNSKEY/NSEC3 and cannot be compared numerically.

dictionary_fields.name: nsec3_iterations
dictionary_fields.description: NSEC3 iteration count (RFC 5155 s3.2, a 16-bit field, 0-65535). Every extra iteration is another SHA-1 pass a validating resolver must perform on a negative answer, which is the root cause of CVE-2023-50868. RFC 9276 recommends 0.

dictionary_fields.name: nsec3_salt
dictionary_fields.description: NSEC3 salt as published. RFC 9276 recommends an empty salt: it adds no security against a modern attacker and costs a zone re-salt to change.

dictionary_fields.name: rr_type
dictionary_fields.description: DNS resource record type of the observed response record (DNSKEY, DS, RRSIG, NSEC, NSEC3, NSEC3PARAM, CDS, CDNSKEY, ...).

dictionary_fields.name: rrsig_type_covered
dictionary_fields.description: RR type an RRSIG covers (RFC 4034 s3.1.1). Present only on RRSIG records, so it evidences the RFC 4034 signature record format directly.

dictionary_fields.name: rsa_key_bitsize
dictionary_fields.description: Modulus size of an RSA DNSKEY/CDNSKEY in bits. Carries the operational key-strength signal RFC 6781 discusses; null for every non-RSA algorithm, which is itself informative.

dictionary_fields.name: source
dictionary_fields.description: OpenINTEL measurement source / partition identifier (e.g. the zone file or top list the name was drawn from).

dictionary_fields.name: timestamp
dictionary_fields.description: Measurement timestamp (UTC) at which the DNS response was observed.

dictionary_fields.name: tlsa_matchtype
dictionary_fields.description: TLSA matching type (RFC 6698 s2.1.3): 0 exact, 1 SHA-256, 2 SHA-512.

dictionary_fields.name: tlsa_selector
dictionary_fields.description: TLSA selector (RFC 6698 s2.1.2): 0 full certificate, 1 SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

dictionary_fields.name: tlsa_usage
dictionary_fields.description: TLSA certificate usage (RFC 6698 s2.1.1): 0 PKIX-TA, 1 PKIX-EE, 2 DANE-TA, 3 DANE-EE. RFC 7671 gives operational guidance that favours 2 and 3.

dictionary_fields.name: zone
dictionary_fields.description: Zone or TLD the measurement partition belongs to.
